item.text: {"question_id":"1B.9","answer":"Egypt established a National Council for Artificial Intelligence and launched the Egyptian Charter for Responsible AI in April 2023. The charter set values and implementation guidance, contemplated impact assessments for government AI projects, MCIT supervision and periodic reporting to the Council, and annual review. This is favorable formal evidence, but the charter was non-binding, supervision was stated as something projects should receive rather than shown as a universally enforced requirement, and the supplied record shows no funding, inspections, completed assessments, enforcement actions, reports, or review outcomes. Cyber-risk exposure was substantial: international hacking teams targeted government institutions for espionage and data theft in 2023, while Egyptian law restricted encryption, enabled data retention and access without judicial orders, and left a data-protection law suspended for missing executive regulations. These legal and surveillance measures were government policies under Sisi's administration, but the evidence does not establish his personal direction of each measure or a specific response to the external attacks. A government-linked university-application process also exposed personal data of more than 72,000 children for at least eight months, without supplied evidence of an official investigation or remedy. Environmental and resource-governance evidence indicates broader weaknesses in implementation, monitoring, funding, and transparency, but it is not treated as direct evidence of AI, cyber, biological, or other dual-use safeguards absent a demonstrated catastrophic pathway. Overall, the record shows a prospective AI governance framework and some formal review concepts, alongside weakly demonstrated enforceability, transparency, cyber safeguards, and implementation; biological-risk, advanced-cyber-defense, AI-incident, laboratory-biosafety, and catastrophic-risk budget evidence remains unavailable.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0020-E001","BATCH-0020-E002","BATCH-0019-E016","BATCH-0009-R02-E017","BATCH-0009-R02-E019","BATCH-0009-R07-E012"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0009-R01-E013","BATCH-0009-R02-E021","BATCH-0009-R10-E003","BATCH-0009-R10-E004","BATCH-0009-R10-E014","BATCH-0009-R10-E016","BATCH-0009-R10-E017"],"limitations_and_gaps":["No biological-risk, laboratory-biosafety, advanced-cyber-defense, AI-incident, catastrophic-risk budget, enforcement, inspection, or completed-review evidence is supplied.","The AI charter is non-binding; its proposed supervision, impact assessments, periodic reporting, and annual review are not shown to have been implemented or enforced during 2023.","The external cyberattacks and child-data exposure establish risk exposure and governance concerns but do not by themselves prove Sisi's personal knowledge, direction, or response.","Environmental and climate evidence is contextual only because the supplied record does not establish a specific catastrophic dual-use pathway."],"corrections_made":["Added the omitted 2023 government-institution cyberattacks and broader cyber-threat context.","Added encryption restrictions, surveillance and data-access powers, data retention, and the suspended data-protection framework.","Separated external cyber exposure from ruler-attributable performance and preserved attribution limits.","Reduced the weight of ordinary environmental and resource-governance evidence, retaining it only as contextual evidence about implementation and transparency weaknesses.","Qualified the AI charter's supervision language and distinguished formal design from demonstrated enforcement or outcomes."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["A full review would be warranted if evidence of biological safeguards, cyber-defense investment, AI-project audits, incident response, laboratory controls, or actual implementation of the charter becomes available.","The personal attribution of surveillance, data-protection non-implementation, and responses to the 2023 government cyberattacks remains incomplete."]}
